peat_hermit.text: Och! You crossed the bog? In those boots? Come in, come in. I haven't had a visitor since the last ice age.

then.text: I gave you the cranachan already. It's whisky-free, I'm assured. Mostly raspberries. Mind how you go back across.

else.text: Take this. It's cranachan, toasted oats, cream and raspberries. I make it with a spoon, a bowl and no sense of urgency.

reindeer.text: It sniffs your sleeve for lichen, finds none, and goes back to being majestic. A very big pair of antlers sways, gently.

reindeer_herder.text: Each reindeer has a name and a rude personality. Frost, Bramble, Bagpipes. That one's called Dolly. She's not very polite.
Reindeer hooves click when they walk, a sound like castanets. It helps the herd stay together in a blizzard. The best part of my job is the herd. The worst bit is the blizzards.

then.text: Seven. Of course it was seven. Five at the paddock and two who've wandered off to be dramatic. That's what I wrote in the book.
How many reindeer have you counted on this stretch?
Seven! The five at the paddock and the two out on the hills! You've the eye. Here, for your trouble. Cranachan, the proper sort. It has real oats in it.

else.text: Hmm. That's not the number in my book. Have another look: the ones at the paddock, and the shy ones out on the hills. All of them count.
I'm one short in my sums this year, or one over. Would you count them for me? Every reindeer on this stretch, paddock and hill, then come back and tell me.

ski_instructor.text: Scotland has skiing! The snow isn't always there, but when it is, it's glorious. And when it isn't, I teach people to fall over in a dignified way.
Cairn Gorm has the UK's highest funicular railway, running up to near the summit. We love it dearly. It was also closed for years for repairs. The affection was constant, the railway less so.

rescue_volunteer.text: Mountain Rescue here is volunteers, who go out in all weathers for anyone who needs them. We are not paid and not grateful for puns about 'rocks'.
The golden rules: tell someone where you're going, carry a map, a compass and a head torch. And never trust a cloud that looks friendly.

snow_kid.text: I made a snowman! He's got a pine cone for a nose and a wooden spoon for a sceptre. I call him Sir Ben Macdui. He's the second-highest snowman in Britain.

Ben Macdui's the second highest mountain in the UK, and legend says there's a tall grey man up there. Not a snowman. A 'Big Grey Man'. People hear his footsteps. I hear mine. It's the same thing, probably.

arts_shepherd_reader.text: {greeting} Nan Shepherd says the mountain is not a thing you climb, it is a thing you go into. I have been going into it since breakfast and I am still not out.
The Living Mountain sat in a drawer for thirty years because no publisher wanted a book about walking slowly. Now it is on every reading list in Scotland. Drawers are underrated.
She is on the five-pound note. I like to think she is still paying for the bus.
